findings.explanation: The new endpoint GET /users/<user_id>/orders authenticates the caller with @require_auth but then queries Order by the request-supplied user_id with no ownership verification. Any authenticated user can pass an arbitrary user_id and retrieve that user's orders (including shipping_address), violating security-policy.md §3 ('A user may view ONLY their own orders... Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators') and api-spec.md which lists '/users/<id>/orders | GET | owner or admin'. The sibling endpoint get_user in the same file correctly gates on is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id) (users.py:32), and the policy mandates using is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) for order access. The new code omits this check entirely.

evidence.content: A user may view ONLY their own orders. Every endpoint that fetches an order by its identifier MUST verify ownership with is_owner_or_admin(current_user, order.user_id) before returning data. Listing another user's orders is restricted to that user themselves and administrators.

findings.suggested_fix: Add an ownership check before querying: `if not is_owner_or_admin(g.current_user, user_id): return jsonify({"error": "forbidden"}), 403` at the start of user_orders, matching the pattern used in get_user.

args.query: require_auth, require_role, is_owner_or_admin decorators in app/auth
